name: Crucible Industries Cerberus-357 'Hellhound'
description:
The Crucible Industries Cerberus-357 is a six-shot double-action revolver chambered in .357 Magnum, featuring three barrels arranged in a triangular cluster. The weapon fires from a single cylinder through whichever barrel is aligned by the rotary barrel selector — the shooter can choose between a standard four-inch barrel, a two-inch barrel for close-quarters work, and a six-inch barrel with a target crown for precision shots. Barrel selection is controlled by a thumb switch on the frame.

The Cerberus is an engineering exercise that somehow became a production weapon. Crucible's design team originally built the triple-barrel prototype as a proof of concept for a military contract that required a single sidearm adaptable to multiple engagement ranges. The contract fell through, but the prototype generated enough interest that Crucible produced a commercial run. The resulting weapon is mechanically complex, heavier than a conventional revolver, and undeniably versatile.

The Hellhound has a cult following among operators who appreciate mechanical ingenuity and don't mind carrying extra weight. The ability to switch between barrels mid-engagement — close range, then stepping back to the precision barrel — provides tactical flexibility that no other revolver offers. Whether that flexibility justifies the weight and complexity is a matter of ongoing debate in firearms forums that generates thousands of comments and zero consensus.
specifications:
caliber: .357 Magnum
effective_range: 15-60 meters (barrel dependent)
rate_of_fire: Double-action revolver
magazine_capacity: 6 rounds (cylinder)
weight: 1.38 kg
tactical_use: A versatile revolver offering three engagement profiles in a single weapon. The two-inch barrel provides maximum maneuverability at close range, the four-inch barrel suits general-purpose use, and the six-inch barrel enables precision shooting. Barrel switching takes approximately one second via the thumb selector. The added weight and mechanical complexity are trade-offs for the unique multi-range capability.
cultural_context: The Hellhound is the firearms equivalent of a conversation starter — nobody sees one without asking about it, and nobody who carries one gets tired of explaining it. In weapon culture, it occupies a space reserved for objects that are simultaneously brilliant and slightly absurd. People either love it or think it's the most over-engineered solution to a problem nobody had.
story_hooks: A Cerberus is found at a crime scene with one barrel recently fired and two clean — but the ballistics match all three barrels at three different crime scenes over three days. Someone is cleaning two barrels after each use.
Crucible Industries announces a four-barrel Cerberus prototype and offers it as a prize in a competition that turns out to be far more dangerous than the entry form suggested.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist engineering statement — three barrels splayed in a distinct triangular cluster from a heavily reinforced frame, immediately marking it as unconventional. The silhouette is wider and denser than a standard revolver, with the triple-barrel arrangement dominating the front profile. Despite its complexity, it maintains a coherent, almost organic geometry reminiscent of its namesake.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length 22-28 cm (barrel-dependent alignment). Frame width at barrel cluster: 8.5 cm. Cylinder diameter: 4.2 cm. Two-inch barrel: 5 cm. Four-inch barrel: 10 cm. Six-inch barrel: 15 cm. Barrel cluster projection: 6 cm forward of frame.
physical_description.weight_description: Decidedly hefty — 1.38 kg with substantial forward weight bias. Feels planted and grounded in the hand, with the triple-barrel cluster creating noticeable muzzle-heavy characteristics. Requires confident grip strength; not a weapon for casual carry or quick-draw specialists.
physical_description.primary_material: Hardened steel frame and barrel cluster with aerospace-grade aluminum alloy receiver housing. Cylinder of tool steel with precision-bored chambers.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal grey with selective brushed steel accents on the barrel cluster edges. Visible machine marks and precision-cut cooling grooves along the barrel housing. Minimal polish — engineering over aesthetics.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey primary with brushed chrome/steel highlights on barrel selector mechanism and cylinder release. Accent: deep burnt orange/copper oxidation patina developing on higher-wear edges (intentional or age-dependent).
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured synthetic polymer grip with fine crosshatch pattern for secure purchase despite the weapon's forward weight. Thumb selector positioned for ergonomic rotation — slightly raised, knurled surface for positive feedback.
distinctive_features: Triangular triple-barrel cluster with visible spacing grooves for heat dissipation
Rotary barrel selector thumb switch with click-stop detents (3-position)
Precision-machined barrel alignment channels visible on frame sides
Crucible Industries maker's mark stamped on frame above trigger guard
Serial plate inset into right grip panel with enhanced registration ID overlay
Visible torque wrench marks on triple-barrel assembly bolts
Cooling vents machined into barrel cluster housing
Target crown visible on six-inch barrel (slight beveled edge)
Custom engravings: 'CERBERUS-357 HELLHOUND' script along cylinder spine
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Veterinary Genomics serif logo stamped above trigger guard. 'CERBERUS-357 | HELLHOUND' engraved along the cylinder spine in angled modern sans-serif. Enhanced registration hologram embedded in right grip panel (reflects light at specific angles). Model number etched on frame base beneath cylinder.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained condition — clean barrel bores from regular use, light fingerprint oils on grip, minor scratch patterns on selector mechanism from repeated thumb operation. Muzzle edges show subtle wear from hundreds of draws. No rust, but atmospheric oxidation patina is expected and considered characteristic.
